hypothesis: In female plaice of fixed length, weight-at-length is lowest around March–April and highest around November, and the weight loss is accounted for by spawning, so gonad weight and maturity stage track the seasonal cycle and mark the spawning season.
pass_criterion: Using mature females, fit log(W_fish) = a + b*log(L_fish) + month effect. PASS if all three hold. (1) Length-adjusted weight in Mar–Apr is at least 8% lower than in Nov (or the nearest sampled autumn month), with p<0.05. (2) The month of minimum length-adjusted weight falls in Feb–Apr and the month of maximum falls in Oct–Dec. (3) Monthly mean gonad weight fraction (W_gon/W_fish) covaries with monthly mean length-adjusted weight (Spearman |rho| > 0.5), and the spawning period indicated by maturity stage (mat_estim) agrees with the weight minimum to within one month.
fail_criterion: FAIL if the length-adjusted weight difference between Mar–Apr and Nov is under 3% or not significant (p>=0.05). FAIL also if the minimum is outside Jan–May, or if the gonad weight fraction does not covary with length-adjusted weight (|rho| < 0.3), which would mean spawning does not explain the cycle. If the dates do not cover both the Nov–Apr fall and the May–Nov recovery, the result is reported as inconclusive, not as a pass.
interpretation: 'Weight at unchanging length' is read as the residual from a length-weight regression (or Fulton's K). 'Bulk' is read as total body weight. 'Spawning and rebuilding of tissues and reproductive organs' is read as the gonad weight fraction (W_gon/W_fish) and visual maturity stage (mat_estim). 'Determined from length and weight alone' is tested by checking that the month of minimum residual weight coincides with the spawning period given by the gonad data. Caveats: the dataset holds 151 females from the French Eastern Channel, sampled in 2017–2019. Its catch months are in the Date column of Macros.csv, which I did not see on the landing page, so seasonal coverage is unconfirmed and may be partial. It has no males. Feeding and temperature also affect condition, so 'wholly' is tested as the share of seasonal variance in residual weight that gonad weight accounts for.
